wizard.resumeBody: You'd got as far as {step}. Nothing was lost — carry on from there.

w1.title: What does {business} do?
w1.lede: This loads a starting point that already fits — typical hours, the questions your customers actually ask, and a few rules. You can change every part of it.

w2.title: When are you open?
w2.lede: We've filled in the usual hours. Change whatever isn't right.
w2.after: What should Subiza do when you're closed?
w2.ah1d: It tells them your hours and where you are, then takes their name and what they wanted.
w2.ah2: Answer, and book them for the next open day
w2.ah2d: The same, but it can also hold a slot for them.
w2.ah3d: No answers at all outside your hours — it only collects names.

w3.title: What do you charge?
w3.lede: Price is what callers ask about more than anything else. Without it, Subiza takes a message instead of answering — which works, but it's the difference between useful and impressive.
w3.photoP: Most businesses have a printed list on the wall. Take a picture of it — that is far easier than typing it on a phone.
w3.frame: The whole list is in frame
w3.onDevice: This happens on your phone. Nothing is sent until the photo is good enough to be worth the data.
w3.blurryP: Move a little closer, hold steady, and keep your own shadow off the sheet. We caught this before spending any of your data.
w3.sendingP: Carry on — we'll tell you when it's done.
w3.believe: This is what Subiza now believes your prices are
w3.three: Only the unclear rows need you
w3.threeP: The rest we're confident about. These we couldn't read cleanly, and a price is the one thing we will never guess at.
w3.typeH: Type the ones customers ask about most
w3.none: I don't have a price list

w4.title: How should it sound?
w4.lede: Tap any of them to listen. Each one says your actual greeting, with your actual business name — not a demo sentence.
w4.silentP: Your phone may be on silent, or the browser may be holding audio back until you tap. Turn the volume up and tap play again.
w4.clone: Or use your own voice — later, it needs a separate consent

w5.title: Now hear it yourself.
w5.lede: Subiza is about to ring your phone. Be a customer and ask it whatever a customer would.
w5.ringing: It's ringing now. When you hear the greeting, ask it something.
w5.hang: Hang up whenever you're done. All of this is being kept.
w5.missedP: No problem. There are two other ways to do this, and one of them doesn't need your phone at all.
w5.browser: Talk to it here in the browser
w5.q2: “Are you open on Sunday?” — it knows you're closed
w5.q3: Ask it something you never told it. Watch what it does.
w5.neverRangP: That isn't the only way to do this. There are two others, and neither needs anything to change on your phone.
w5.triedP: The network didn't put the call through. That is usually the network, not your phone.
w5.dialP: Call it whenever you like. Your agent answers, and what you say will appear here.
w5.works: Works for the next day. It costs you nothing.
w5.webP: This is an easier test than the real one. It tests what it says — it does not test how well it hears.
w5.micH: Your browser is about to ask for the microphone
w5.micP: We need to hear you to run the test. Nothing is kept unless you ask us to keep it.
w5.micNoP: That choice lives in your browser. Use either of the other two routes, which ask nothing of this device.
w5.rate: That's a lot of test calls
w5.rateP: You can call again in 8 minutes.
w5.outage: Test calling isn't working right now
w5.outageP: This is our problem, not yours, and it has nothing to do with your agent. Your agent is not broken.
w5.voicemailP: We hung up so it wouldn't keep talking to a machine.
w5.carrier: The network didn't put the call through
w5.cannotFail: This test is not allowed to fail. If all three routes fail we will know, and a person will call you.

w6.heard: You just heard your own agent answer.
w6.heardP: Everything from here is connecting it to the world.
w6.title: What did it get right?
w6.lede: Read it back. Anything you correct takes effect immediately — it doesn't go into a queue for someone to look at later.
w6.fixH: This corrects your Saturday hours and adds the phrasing to your pronunciation list. Both take effect on the next call.

w7.title: When it can't help, who should it get?
w7.lede: An agent that cannot fetch a human is not allowed to answer your customers. That is the one step in this whole flow you cannot skip.
w7.hint: That's your own number. You can change it, or add other people to the rota later.
w7.refuseP: Subiza needs someone to call when it can't help. Without a number, it can't answer your customers.
w7.n1: Take a message, and tell them when you'll call back
w7.n1d: The customer gets a specific time, not a vague “someone will call you.”
w7.n2d: You'll build the rota of people afterwards.

w8.title: Connect your phone
w8.lede: You keep your number. Your customers keep calling the same one they always have, and Subiza only picks up what you'd have missed.
w8.heading: Dial this on the phone with the SIM
w8.rings: Your phone rings for 20 seconds first, every single time.
w8.plat: Android only, and it never dials by itself. On iPhone this becomes copy-and-paste steps — tap-to-dial links fail silently there.
w8.copyWorks: Copy is the action that works.
w8.checkedP: We just called your number. Subiza picked up after 20 seconds, exactly as it should.
w8.check: I've dialled it — check for me
w8.sandboxP: It just isn't taking real customer calls yet. You can keep testing it as much as you like, and Home will carry this one step until you're ready.

w9.title: How much should it handle?
w9.lede: Start narrow. You widen this yourself, later, when it has earned it — and you can narrow it again in one tap.
w9.r1d: Every call during your hours still comes to you. Evenings and Sundays, it answers. There is no downside to this one, because right now those calls ring out to nobody.
w9.r2d: Your phone rings first every time. Subiza picks up after 20 seconds, or when you're on another call.
w9.r3d: It answers first, always, and fetches you the moment a customer needs a person.

home.title: That's it. Your agent is answering.
home.sandboxTitle: Your agent is ready to test.
home.lede: Everything below is optional and none of it is urgent. Here's where you've got to.
home.waD: Meta takes 5–15 working days — worth starting today
home.cloneD: Needs audio and a separate consent
home.creditD: Your free allowance is still fine
home.paused: Calls are going to you now. The agent is paused.

aside.w1a: Why this is the first question
aside.w1ap: A blank page is the single most common reason a non-technical person abandons setup. Six choices load a real starting point, and the panel shows you exactly what arrived.
aside.w1bp: These six are distinguishable in two seconds, which is the test that actually matters.
aside.w2a: The most valuable thing Subiza does
aside.w2ap: It answers at nine on a Sunday evening. That's why hours come this early — they draw the boundary that frames the whole product.
aside.w2bp: We never say this will take a long time. The marks show where you are, never a countdown.
aside.w3a: A price is a field, not a paragraph
aside.w3ap: A price is a typed row: read out loud, never generated.
aside.w3bp: Sharpness, glare and framing are checked on the device before a single byte is uploaded.
aside.w4ap: Every preview says your actual greeting with your actual business name.
aside.w4bp: Audio only plays when you tap. An autoplaying preview is silently blocked on most first visits.
aside.w5a: This is the screen that matters
aside.w5ap: Activation is hearing your own agent answer a question about your own business, in your own language, and judging the answer good.
aside.w5b: Three routes, because this step is not allowed to fail
aside.w5bp: We call you. If that fails, you talk to it in the browser. If that fails, you dial a number yourself.
aside.w6a: This is where the product teaches its own mind
aside.w6ap: It answers from what I told it, I can see why, I can fix it, and the fix works immediately.
aside.w7a: The one step that can't be skipped
aside.w7ap: An agent with nowhere to send a customer who needs a person should not be answering the phone at all.
aside.w8a: The one place we genuinely can't help
aside.w8ap: A forwarding code is a command from your SIM. What we can do is call your number and tell you it worked.
aside.w8bp: Skip it and the agent stays fully usable in test mode, with Home carrying exactly one outstanding action.
aside.w9ap: You are being asked to let it pick up the calls that currently ring out — a decision with no downside.
aside.w9bp: We won't nag you to widen it. You can narrow it again in one tap.

console.readonly: You can change this later. This is what activation wrote.
console.whatsappD: Meta verification takes 5–15 working days. Start the request here when you are ready.
console.emptyBody: This is where the phone line and messaging sit once they are set up.
console.offline: This screen is waiting for a connection. Nothing was lost.
console.deniedBody: Someone with the {who} role can change forwarding. The line itself is untouched.
console.rateLimited: The check can run again in {minutes} minutes.
console.errorBody: The last known state is still on the server. Try again, or Aline will call during 08:00–19:00, Monday to Saturday.

phone.g22: Your own phone still rings. Your number is untouched. Nobody was lost.
phone.humanLine: Aline calls you back within fifteen minutes, Monday to Saturday, 08:00–19:00.
phone.s1lede: We recommend the first one every time. It changes nothing for your customers and it works today rather than next week.
phone.pathAd: Your customers keep calling the number they already know. Subiza picks up only what you'd have missed.
phone.pathBd: A separate line just for Subiza. It takes a few days, because the regulator needs your business documents first.
phone.s2title: Which calls should Subiza pick up?
phone.s2lede: This matches what you chose during setup, and you can change it at any time afterwards.
phone.scope1d: No answer, line busy, or phone off. That's three codes dialled one after another — we walk you through all three.
phone.scope2d: One code only. If your phone is busy or off, calls go wherever they went before — usually your voicemail.
phone.scope3d: Your own phone stops ringing entirely. Few businesses want this, but it exists.
phone.allWarnTitle: This stops your own phone ringing
phone.allWarnBody: Unconditional forwarding means every call goes to Subiza immediately. That is a live reachability change. Dial ##21# if you want your phone to ring again.
phone.s3lede: Only the handset holding the SIM can do this. No website — including ours — can send this command for you.
phone.netUnknown: The network is not clear from this prefix
phone.vmBody: A line can only forward each condition to one place. Right now that's your carrier's voicemail; after this code it's Subiza. Dial *#61# first if you want to see what's there now.
phone.codeNote: Your phone rings for 20 seconds first, every time. Only after that does Subiza pick up.
phone.copyWorks: Copy is the action that works.
phone.platAndroid: Android only, and it never dials by itself.
phone.platIos: On iPhone, tap-to-dial links fail silently — use the three steps.
phone.ios3: Paste it and call. Tap-to-dial links fail silently on iPhone.
phone.explain: What does this code actually say?
phone.ex61: “Register a forwarding destination for no reply.” 61 is the international service code for that condition.
phone.exN: The Subiza number. It's the only part of this string that belongs to you.
phone.ex11: “Voice calls only.” We send it because every carrier document does. The standard also allows skipping it with a doubled star — that shorter shape is on the next screen if this one is refused.
phone.ex20: Wait 20 seconds before diverting. The standard allows 5 to 30, in steps of five. We fixed it at 20 so the string has one fewer thing a switch can reject.
phone.undoHere: To undo later: ##002# clears every forward. Per condition: ##61#, ##67#, ##62#.
phone.s4lede: We'll call your number now. Don't answer it — let it ring, so we can watch where the call ends up.
phone.still: The last check is still on screen. The radio may have dropped during the call — that is expected.
phone.retryWait: The first check did not see a divert. The network gets sixty seconds, then we watch once more — automatically.
phone.okBody: Calls you don't answer now reach Subiza. There is nothing else you need to do.
phone.ownerTitle: You picked up — which is exactly right
phone.ownerBody: That's what should happen: your phone rings first. But to check the diversion itself, we need it to ring out. Let it ring this time.
phone.cliTitle: It's working — but the caller's number doesn't come through
phone.cliBody: Subiza is answering properly. What it can't see is who's calling, so it won't recognise a returning customer and it can't put their number in the message it sends you. Everything else works.
phone.cliNote: We've recorded this on your account and we'll tell you if it changes.
phone.badBody: We called, your phone rang, and the call never arrived here. This is not something you did wrong — these codes fail on the network more often than anyone admits.
phone.mmiBody: That message comes from the handset or the network, not from us, and it does not mean you typed it wrong. There are several other shapes of the same code.
phone.elseBody: Something answered that was not Subiza — usually the carrier's voicemail, which still owns that condition. Aline can walk through replacing it, Monday to Saturday, 08:00–19:00.
phone.incBody: The result never came back to us. That is our side, not the carrier's, and it is not a reason to change the code. Aline can retry it, or tap Test again.
phone.g22Body: The call came back to us in under eight seconds. That means unconditional forwarding is on, and your own phone is no longer ringing. Dial ##21# now. Aline is on 08:00–19:00, Monday to Saturday, if you want a person on the line.
phone.s6lede: In order, easiest first. Most people are sorted by the second one.
phone.r1d: {code} — no timer, no voice field. Some networks accept only this shape.
phone.r2d: Dial *#61# — your phone will show you whether something is already forwarding, usually voicemail.
phone.r3d: Dial ##002# to erase all forwarding, then dial ours again. Conflicts between old settings are a common cause.
phone.r4: Have a person call me and walk me through it
phone.r4d: Mon–Sat, 08:00–19:00. We call you back within fifteen minutes.
phone.r4ok: Aline has the full context. You will not need to explain this again. The window is Monday to Saturday, 08:00–19:00.
phone.prepaidTitle: Some prepaid lines can't forward at all
phone.prepaidBody: That's a carrier policy rather than a fault on your handset. Aline will call and confirm — and a new Subiza number is the usual answer when it happens.
phone.s7lede: Here's exactly what's in place, and how to undo any of it.
phone.offBody: One code clears every forward. Calls go straight back to your own phone, and your number is untouched. Individually: ##61#, ##67#, ##62#.
phone.costBody: On a standard GSM line the diverting subscriber — you — pays for the forwarded leg, as if you'd made that call. We don't yet know MTN and Airtel Rwanda's actual rate for it, and we won't invent one. The moment we've measured it, it appears here and in your billing screen.
phone.weekBody: Forwarding lives on your carrier's switch, not with us, and it can vanish without warning — a SIM swap, a handset reset, a network change. We call your number once a week during waking hours, so that if it stops, you hear it from us and not from a customer.
phone.s8title: A new number takes a few days
phone.s8lede: This isn't us being slow. The regulator requires your business documents before a number can be issued, and we would rather say “three to seven days” than “instant” and then disappoint you on day four.
phone.tl1d: RDB certificate, your ID, your address — collected once
phone.tl2d: This is the wait. We can't shorten it and we won't pretend to
phone.tl3d: From what's available at the time
phone.tl4d: Same as everything else — we check before we say it works
phone.s8okp: Your agent exists, you can keep testing it, adding prices and getting it right. The number is the only thing waiting. Your existing number is untouched throughout.
phone.orKeep: Or keep my own number instead, and start today
phone.lostLede: This usually follows a SIM swap, a new handset, or a carrier-side reset. Nothing you did caused it.
phone.lostBannerP: We found this during a routine check. Since then, calls you don't answer haven't been reaching Subiza — they've been ringing out or going to your voicemail as before.
phone.lostFoot: Throughout all of this your calls have still reached your own phone. Nobody was lost — they just weren't answered for you.

phoneAside.s1a: Why forwarding, not a new number
phoneAside.s1ap: No porting, no regulatory bundle, no waiting, and the number on your shop sign and your business cards keeps working. But there's a better reason than any of those.
phoneAside.s1bp: Conditional forwarding means every call Subiza handles is, by definition, a call the business would otherwise have lost. That's the number that renews the subscription — and it falls out of the setup choice rather than being estimated.
phoneAside.s2ap: No answer, busy and unreachable are three separate conditions on the carrier's switch, each with its own code. Most businesses want all three, so we present it as one choice and walk you through the three dials.
phoneAside.s2bp: The standard allows anywhere from 5 to 30 seconds. We picked 20 and fixed it, because every extra variable in the string is another thing a network can reject — and a rejected code costs far more than a perfectly-tuned ring time gains.
phoneAside.s3a: The one place we genuinely cannot help
phoneAside.s3ap: There is no API that sets call forwarding on an arbitrary GSM handset. Not one we haven't built — one that does not exist. So the goal here isn't automation; it's making a fifteen-second manual action feel trivial and get rewarded immediately.
phoneAside.s3bp: On Android, a tel: link opens the dialler with the code in it — it never dials by itself. On iPhone, MMI codes in tel: links fail silently; Apple has acknowledged it and not fixed it. So copy is the action that works everywhere.
phoneAside.s3cp: Carrier voicemail is implemented with exactly this mechanism. A line can hold one destination per condition, so registering ours silently replaces theirs. Nobody warns people about this. We do, before they dial, because finding out later feels like something was taken.
phoneAside.s4ap: Every comparable product we looked at asks the customer to call themselves to check. Not one of them verifies it. We place the call, watch where it lands, and tell you.
phoneAside.s4bp: No-answer forwarding only fires when the phone rings out. If you pick up, there's nothing to observe — which is why “you answered” is a neutral result with a friendly retry, not a red error.
phoneAside.s5ap: It worked. You answered. It didn't divert. It diverted but the caller's number was lost. Something else answered. Our own check dropped. The last two are easy to lie about, and we will not.
phoneAside.s5b: We never make it your fault
phoneAside.s5bp: “Invalid MMI code” appears regularly on codes that are entirely correct — it comes from the handset or the switch. Our copy says so, because telling someone they got it wrong when they didn't is how you lose them at the last step.
phoneAside.s6ap: Shorter code, then look at what's already there, then clear everything, then a person. Each step is cheaper than the next, and the last one is always a human — because a rescue here costs us less than a lost customer.
phoneAside.s6bp: Some prepaid plans don't permit call forwarding at all. When that's the answer, a new Subiza number is the fix — and we say so rather than making someone try the same code five times.
phoneAside.s7a: The undo code is shown up front
phoneAside.s7ap: Someone who knows how to reverse a change is far more willing to make it. Hiding the exit doesn't increase retention; it increases hesitation. So ##002# is on this screen, in Settings, and in the connection summary, permanently.
phoneAside.s7b: The silent failure is the dangerous one
phoneAside.s7bp: A business that believes it's covered and isn't is worse off than one we never checked. Weekly re-verification is cheap and it's the only defence, because forwarding is state held by someone else that can disappear with no signal at all.
phoneAside.s8ap: Number provisioning is programmatic but gated on regulatory approval, which is not instant in this region and often involves a human on the other side. Promising instant and delivering four days is how trust is lost in week one.
phoneAside.s9ap: We call your number once a week during waking hours and watch where it lands. It's a small cost, and it is the only method available — no operator in this market exposes an API that could simply be asked.
phoneAside.s9bp: We didn't quietly note it in a dashboard. The message reached you before the shop opened — because the only thing worse than this failing is you finding out from a customer.

channel.deniedTitle: Connecting a channel stays with the owner or a manager
channel.deniedBody: A recovered session, or a role that cannot connect, cannot start this. Channel health is still visible on Connections.
channel.hubTitle: Where do your customers message you?
channel.hubLede: None of these are needed for Subiza to answer your phone — that already works. Connect only the ones your customers actually use, whenever suits you.
channel.hubOrder: The order matters. Telegram first because it proves the messaging side works with zero friction; WhatsApp next because it's the most valuable and the slowest, so its clock should start early.
channel.tgDetail: Two minutes. No review, no waiting, nothing to pay
channel.waDetail: Ten minutes of your time, then Meta takes {minDays}–{maxDays} working days
channel.igDetail: Five minutes. Needs a professional account
channel.webDetail: Copy a snippet, or just take a link
channel.smsDetail: Three weeks. MTN and Airtel register sender IDs separately
channel.tg1lede: Telegram needs a bot of its own for your business. Since 2026 that's one tap rather than a conversation with another bot.
channel.tg1hs: We send a request; you approve it
channel.tg1s1: Tap the button below. Telegram opens
channel.tg1s2: You approve creating the bot — one tap
channel.tg1s3: We receive the token and set everything up
channel.tgOlder: My Telegram is an older version
channel.tg2lede: On older Telegram versions you create the bot by messaging BotFather. Copy these exactly as they are.
channel.tg2c5: Copy the token it sends back
channel.tg2hint: We check it as you paste and show you your bot straight back.
channel.tg2bad: That token was not accepted. Paste the one BotFather sent, in full.
channel.wa1lede: Meta runs most of this and we don't control it. These three questions exist so that we never walk you into a wall inside a window we can't fix.
channel.wa1q2: Is that number already on WhatsApp, or WhatsApp Business?
channel.wa1q2d: This is the question that stops most people. A number that's live in either app can't just be registered — but there are three ways round it, and we'd rather show you them now than inside Meta's popup.
channel.wa1q3: Is your business registered with RDB?
channel.wa1q3d: Meta requires business documents. If you don't have them yet, every other channel still works — WhatsApp is the only one that asks.
channel.wa2title: Three ways forward, and none of them is right for everyone.
channel.wa2lede: This is a business judgement rather than a technical one, so here are the real trade-offs rather than a recommendation.
channel.wa2moved: Delete it from the WhatsApp Business app, then register it for the API.
channel.wa2moveb: Old chats stay on the phone, and the app stops working for that number
channel.wa2coexd: Keep using the WhatsApp Business app and let Subiza work on the same number.
channel.wa2coexg: You keep the app you already know
channel.wa2coexb1: {history} days of history, synced once — and it must finish within {window} hours
channel.wa2coexb2: Only media from the last {media} days comes across
channel.wa2coexb3: Groups, status and calls are invisible to Subiza entirely
channel.wa2coexb4: Throughput is capped at {mps} messages a second
channel.wa2otherd: A second SIM, or a new number, used only by Subiza.
channel.wa2otherg: Technically the simplest of the three by far
channel.wa2otherb: You have to tell your customers a new number
channel.wa3once: This can only be done once. If it doesn't finish inside the coexistence window it cannot be retried — the number has to be fully removed and the whole signup started again from the beginning.
channel.wa3title: What you need to do for the next {window} hours
channel.wa3k1: Leave WhatsApp Business open on your phone
channel.wa3k1d: It's the app that sends the history across. Closed, everything stops
channel.wa3k2d: Today, then later, then the full {history} days
channel.wa3k3d: Groups, status and calls never come across
channel.wa3rw: We're not certain this is available in Rwanda yet
channel.wa3rwd: Meta added coexistence for Nigeria and South Africa in April 2026 and has been rolling it out country by country. If it turns out not to be live for your number, we'll tell you as soon as we know and move you to one of the other two routes — you won't discover it halfway through.
channel.wa3rwOff: Coexistence is not live for this number. We'll move you to one of the other two routes — you won't discover it halfway through.
channel.wa3back: Take me back to the other routes
channel.wa4lede: Their window is about to open. We've pre-filled everything we already know so there's less to type. Here's what it will ask.
channel.wa4hs: We can't see inside them and we can't change them
channel.wa4s1: Log in to Meta and accept the terms
channel.wa4s2: Choose or create your business portfolio
channel.wa4s3: The WhatsApp account, your number, and the name customers will see — pre-filled by us
channel.wa4s4: The SMS code that arrives on that number
channel.wa4plat: Have that phone in your hand now. We cannot receive that code for you — nobody can, and any product claiming otherwise is describing something else.
channel.wa4nojs: Meta's window needs a browser that can open it
channel.wa4nojsD: Everything around this screen still works. Telegram can be connected now; WhatsApp waits until you have a browser that can open Meta's window.
channel.wa4expired: The signup code expired after {ttl} seconds
channel.wa4expiredD: We never retry an expired code. Open the window again and we'll start a new one.
channel.wa5expTitle: The signup code expired after {ttl} seconds
channel.wa5expBody: We never retry an expired exchange. Here is a plain explanation and a relaunch — not a raw error.
channel.wa5got: You'd got as far as {where}. That's the most common place to stop, usually because the SMS took longer than expected.
channel.wa5h1: We'll start it again — but now you know what's coming
channel.wa5lede: Meta doesn't let anyone resume mid-window — it restarts from the beginning, for everyone. What we can do is tell you exactly where you stopped and what to have ready this time.
channel.wa5prepd: Have the phone with that SIM in your hand. The SMS can take a couple of minutes. The window doesn't like you leaving it to go and look.
channel.wa6lede: The rest is Meta's, and nobody can speed it up. Here's where it actually stands, with real timeframes rather than comfortable ones.
channel.wa6queueD: New WhatsApp connections share a weekly pool until our own verification completes. This number is the real position, not an estimate.
channel.wa6k2d: Until it's approved, customers see your number instead of your name. Messaging still works
channel.wa6k3d: Your documents, submitted once and reused everywhere
channel.wa6k4d: This is the hard one in this market — see below
channel.wa6ok: Nothing is stopped while you wait
channel.wa6okd: Your phone is being answered today. Telegram works. We message you the moment anything here changes, so there's no reason to come back and check.
channel.wa7bannerD: This does not block anything. Customers see your number for now, and messaging carries on exactly as before.
channel.wa7lede: Meta's reason was emoji and promotional wording. These four things get names rejected more than anything else:
channel.wa7g: A generic word on its own
channel.wa7r: A name that doesn't match your RDB registration
channel.wa7hint: Your registered name, exactly as RDB has it, is the one that always passes.
channel.wa8lede: Meta charges for some message types and bills the business directly, not us. In a market where almost nobody has a card, that is a genuine wall — so here is exactly where it stands.
channel.wa8tiers: Meta has two partner tiers. A Tech Provider cannot pay on its customers' behalf — every business must add its own card. A Solution Partner holds a credit line with Meta, pays Meta directly, and invoices its customers itself.
channel.wa8momo: That means we can pay Meta and you can pay us with MoMo. It is the difference between this channel being available to a Kigali salon and being available only to businesses with international cards — which is why it is a market decision, not a technical one.
channel.wa8now: Right now, a card is needed
channel.wa8nowd: Until we reach that tier, you'll add a payment method in your own Meta account. We'll walk you through it, and we won't pretend it's a small thing.
channel.wa8exit: I don't have a card — let me use the other channels
channel.wa9lede: These are Meta's limits, not ours, and they move on their own depending on how customers react to your messages. Better to know them now than to discover one by failing to send.
channel.wa9start: Messages you can start per day
channel.wa9reply: Replies within {waWindow} hours of a customer writing
channel.wa9rised: When your messages are well received and you've used at least half your allowance in a week, Meta raises the level automatically, usually within hours. You don't apply for it. It also falls the same way if people start blocking you, which is the part nobody mentions.
channel.wa9octd: Until then, replying to customers is free without limit. From that date you get {free} free service messages per number per month, and beyond that they're billed. For a salon this changes nothing at all — but it's true, and you should hear it from us first.
channel.wa9aiP: You may have heard that Meta banned AI on WhatsApp. Here is what their terms actually say:
channel.wa9quote: Providers and developers of artificial intelligence… are strictly prohibited from accessing or using the WhatsApp Business Solution… for the purposes of providing, delivering, offering, selling, or otherwise making available such technologies when such technologies are the primary (rather than incidental or ancillary) functionality being made available for use.
channel.wa9ok: What's banned is using WhatsApp to distribute an AI assistant as the product — a general chatbot people talk to for its own sake. Subiza answers questions about your salon: your hours, your prices, your bookings. That's the ancillary case their terms carve out, and it is explicitly permitted.
channel.ig1title: Your Instagram is a personal account
channel.ig1lede: Instagram doesn't let any software read messages on a personal account. Switching is free, takes about half a minute, and you can switch back whenever you like.
channel.ig1stillD: That's a first-class state, not a failure. Switch in the Instagram app, then check again.
channel.ig1a: How your profile looks to everyone
channel.ig1page: You don't need a Facebook Page. The route we use connects to Instagram directly, which removes the step that used to defeat most people.
channel.ig2title: What Instagram allows, and what it doesn't
channel.ig2lede: Instagram's limits are harder than WhatsApp's and almost nobody explains them. These two shape how the agent behaves.
channel.ig2mig: What we do when the window is closing
channel.ig2migd: If a conversation isn't finished and the {igWindow} hours are nearly up, Subiza offers to move that customer to WhatsApp or SMS. Without that, the conversation simply dies and you never learn you lost someone.
channel.ig2why: Why we don't use the human-agent tag
channel.ig2whyd: It would extend the window, and the API would happily let us set it. But Meta's policy reserves it for messages a real person actually sends. An AI agent using it would be against the rules even though nothing would stop it technically — so we don't.
channel.brkBody: Since {since}, {channel} messages haven't been reaching Subiza. Your phone and the other channels are unaffected and still working normally.
channel.brkP: Since {since}, Instagram messages haven't been reaching Subiza. Your phone and WhatsApp are unaffected and still working normally.
channel.brkLede: The access token expired. Instagram's tokens last {tokenDays} days and we refresh them ahead of time — occasionally one slips past, usually because the account changed something. Nothing you did caused it.
channel.brkHint: Meta never tells anyone when access is revoked — we find out from the first message that fails. That's why the banner names the time we first saw it, rather than pretending we knew earlier than we did.

channelAside.tg1ap: Until recently, creating a bot meant a chat with BotFather and copying a token by hand. Bot API 9.6 added a request the account owner approves with one tap, after which we can fetch the token ourselves.
channelAside.tg1bp: The owner still has to tap. There is no way to create a bot on somebody's behalf without their live consent, and there shouldn't be. What's gone is the copying, not the consent.
channelAside.tg2ap: BotFather is the fallback for older Telegram clients. The token is pasted here once; we never ask you to keep it.
channelAside.tg2bp: If the token is wrong you see that on this page, not after a silent failure later.
channelAside.wa1a: The second question is the whole trick
channelAside.wa1ap: The most-cited failure in every competing WhatsApp product is someone launching Meta's popup, hitting “this number is already in use” inside a window they don't control, and giving up. Asking beforehand turns a dead end into three choices.
channelAside.wa1b: The third prevents a pointless wait
channelAside.wa1bp: Without RDB registration WhatsApp won't complete. Better to learn that in a few seconds than after days of waiting on a verification that was never going to pass.
channelAside.wa2ap: Each route is right for a different business, and guessing on someone's behalf produces regret — especially with coexistence, which can't be undone or retried.
channelAside.wa2b: The bad news is at the top
channelAside.wa2bp: Coexistence's five real limitations are visible before the tap, not after the failure. All five are true and none of them is softened.
channelAside.wa3ap: If the sync does not finish inside the window the number must be fully offboarded and the whole signup redone. That is why the limits sit on this screen, before the tap.
channelAside.wa3bp: If coexistence is not live for the number, we say so on this screen and move to another route. You will not discover it halfway through.
channelAside.wa4a: We can't see inside that window
channelAside.wa4ap: Meta builds it and we can't change a pixel. What we do get is an event naming the screen someone left on, which is why the next screen can say “you got as far as verifying the number” rather than starting blind.
channelAside.wa4bp: Business name, category and number are injected before the window opens. Fewer fields to fill inside Meta's UI means fewer things that can go wrong in the part we don't control.
channelAside.wa5ap: No provider can pick up a mid-window Meta session. So we spend the effort on preparation: phone in hand, SMS may take a minute.
channelAside.wa5bp: The CANCEL event names the screen. That sentence is narrative, not a resume pointer into Meta's flow.
channelAside.wa6a: We can't see inside that window
channelAside.wa6ap: The wait is an opaque interval with a wide, honest range. There is no primary action because there is genuinely nothing to do.
channelAside.wa6bp: The banner is mandatory: the phone is being answered today, and Telegram works. Waiting here is not waiting to be in business.
channelAside.wa7ap: Messaging continues on the number while the name is reviewed again. The four common causes sit on the screen so the next attempt is prepared.
channelAside.wa7bp: The registered name, exactly as RDB has it, is the one that always passes.
channelAside.wa8ap: Until the Solution Partner tier is confirmed, a card is needed and we will not minimise that. The dignified exit is the other channels.
channelAside.wa8bp: A Solution Partner credit line means we pay Meta and you pay us. That decision is recorded, not flipped in this flow.
channelAside.wa9a: Showing the limits is a decision
channelAside.wa9ap: These are Meta's numbers and they move on their own. A tenant who discovers their limit by failing to send has been failed by us, not by Meta — so the number is on the screen from day one.
channelAside.wa9bp: Your customers will have heard about it. The terms ban using WhatsApp to distribute AI as the product, not an agent answering questions about one salon. Better to quote Meta's own words than to leave the question hanging.
channelAside.ig1ap: No software can convert the account. “I've switched — check again” re-reads Instagram. Still personal is a first-class state.
channelAside.ig1bp: The Instagram API with Instagram Login talks to Instagram directly. The older Page step is rejected.
channelAside.ig2a: Instagram is the strictest of the three
channelAside.ig2ap: There is no paid way past the window, and a private reply to a comment can be sent exactly once, ever. Almost no product surfaces either, and both are how businesses silently lose people.
channelAside.ig2b: Not idempotent, so we make it so
channelAside.ig2bp: A second private reply to the same comment returns a hard error, not a quiet no-op. So we record that we've replied before we ever retry — the platform won't protect us, so the product has to.
channelAside.brka: Silent disconnection is the worst failure here
channelAside.brkap: Neither Meta nor Instagram pushes a revocation notice. We find out from the first failed send, mark the channel down, and tell you — because a channel that quietly stops is a business losing customers with no idea it's happening.
channelAside.brkb: One channel down never touches the others
channelAside.brkbp: Instagram is down and the phone and WhatsApp carry on. That isolation is a rule, and it's tested as an acceptance criterion rather than assumed.
